title: Spareware cost model
status: Estimate for planning. Built from price research done on 2026-10-18 and checked independently; every checker correction is applied. Not a quote.
about: What each Spareware app would cost to run, per ride, order, booking, job, sale or active member, and how the at-cost fee falls as more people use it.

currency.tax_note: All figures exclude sales tax. Each country adds its own (GST, VAT or sales tax). The research added 15% NZ GST; it is removed here.

exchange_rates.source: European Central Bank euro reference rates, read through the Frankfurter API
exchange_rates.note: Fixed rates for the currency switch. Prices first priced in EUR, AUD or NZD were converted to USD at these rates. The research used rates of 16 to 18 Oct 2026 (US$1 = NZ$1.7656 to 1.7694), so its NZ$ figures differ from these by under 0.3%.

method.fee_formula: At-cost fee per unit = fixed monthly cost / monthly volume + variable cost per unit. Fixed = servers and services (the app's own servers plus the shared kit's common items) + the people layer. The card or bank fee is passed through on top, per transaction.
method.low: Cheapest researched setup with light use: small rented servers (OVHcloud Sydney or Auckland, Hetzner Europe), Cloudflare R2 storage, open-source maps, search and chat run on our own servers, Amazon SES email.
method.high: Dearest researched setup with heavy use: big cloud with a New Zealand region (AWS Auckland or Azure New Zealand North) and paid services (Mapbox, Algolia, Stream Chat, Postmark, Twilio, Sumsub, AWS MediaConvert and Rekognition).
method.mid: For each part (servers and services, maps, messages, ID checks and moderation, people), the geometric mean of its low and high values, the usual middle for estimates that span a 10 to 1,000 times range. A part that costs nothing in the low case also costs nothing in the middle case (the middle uses the free or self-hosted option there). Not a priced setup. Card fees use their own middle rule.

segments.servers: Servers and services: servers, storage, bandwidth, sign-in, monitoring, backups, bookkeeping software, company filing, app store fee
segments.maps: Maps: map tiles, routing and address search
segments.messages: Messages: text messages, email, chat (push notifications are free)
segments.people: People: a small team for support, moderation, bookkeeping and ledger sign-off
segments.payment: Card or bank fee, passed through at cost

pilot_size.note: The research sized servers and the team for a first deployment of 1,000 to 5,000 members and up to about 10,000 jobs a month. Above that the team must grow; how fast is not researched, so the people line is too low at large volumes. Server capacity per user is not load tested.

assumptions: Example amounts chosen for illustration, not prices: ride US$15, food order US$25, stay booking US$300, work job US$500, market sale US$40, rent US$300 a week.

List apps (Stay, Home, Rent, Work, Market): 10 active users a month for each booking, listing, letting, job or sale, so the browsing costs of people who look but do not buy are counted. Our assumption, not researched.
Spare Rent: the one-off letting cost is spread over a 12-month tenancy. Our assumption.
Each app is costed as if it runs on its own deployment. Ride and Food can share one, and so can the five list apps, which lowers each app's fixed cost.

Member apps (Social, Office, Construct, Studio, OS) carry a per-member server share sized for capacity as well as the small fixed set of servers, so the fixed servers are counted twice at small scale. This errs high.
Free tiers are ignored, as in the research, except where noted. They make a small first deployment cheaper than shown.
Driver, courier, host and trade ID checks are one-off per worker, not per job, and are left out of the per-job figures (US$0 to US$1.35 each).

Paid map APIs are not in the planned design (the kit map uses open map data). If the apps used them, a ride would cost US$0.02 to US$0.29 more with Mapbox or US$0.06 to US$0.67 more with Google Maps Platform (research workings).
not_included: Legal advice, insurance and licences (for example a passenger service licence)
Outside security review before launch (no public price found)
Card disputes (NZ$25 each at Stripe) and refunds
Currency conversion margins on paying offshore suppliers
Growth of the team beyond a pilot
Optional AI use in the design tools (bring your own model costs nothing; light use US$0.30, heavy use US$30 a member a month on Claude API prices)

kit.what: Common items every app deployment needs, on top of its own servers.

items.item: Off-site backup copy, 100 GB on Backblaze B2 (US$6.95 per TB)
Bookkeeping software (example: Xero NZ Ignite NZ$37, Grow NZ$89, ex GST)
Company annual filing (example: NZ Companies Office, NZ$57.20 a year incl GST)
Monitoring and error tracking (low: self-hosted and free plans; high: Grafana Pro US$19 + Sentry Team US$29)
DDoS protection and firewall (low: Cloudflare Free; high: Cloudflare Pro US$25)
Sign-in server (low: self-hosted Keycloak; high: Zitadel Pro US$100)
Apple Developer Program, US$99 a year (only if a native iPhone app ships)
Text message sender number (Twilio international number, US$1.15)
Email plan (high only: Postmark Basic US$15)

account_messages_per_member_usd.workings: Low: 4 emails on Amazon SES at US$0.0001. High: 10 emails at Postmark's US$0.0018 overage + 2 sign-in texts at Twilio's US$0.105. Added to member apps only.

original_nzd_incl_gst.fixed_high_checker: 948.85, plus about 14.77 for two public IPv4 addresses

people.what: A small team for support, moderation, bookkeeping and signing off the cost ledger. Legal and outside accountant time not included.

workings.low: 10 hours a week (support 5, moderation 3, bookkeeping and ledger 2) x 52/12 weeks x NZ$23.95 adult minimum wage (from 1 April 2026) = NZ$1,037.83, x 1.1261 on-costs = NZ$1,168.71
workings.high: 35 hours a week (support 20, moderation 10, accounting 5) x 52/12 x NZ$29.90 Living Wage (2026/27) = NZ$4,534.83, x 1.1261 = NZ$5,106.75
workings.on_costs: 8% pay-as-you-go holiday pay, then KiwiSaver 3.5%, ACC work levy 0.69% and Working Safer levy 0.08% on pay including holiday pay: 1.08 x 1.0427 = 1.1261 (the checker's correction; the research used 12.19%)
workings.mid: Geometric mean of low and high

unverified: ACC work levy 0.69% and Working Safer levy 0.08%: the ACC page could not be read; figures from search excerpts
Team size is a planning assumption for a pilot

payment.what: Card and bank fees are passed through at cost, per transaction. They usually make up most of the at-cost fee. They differ by country and provider; the example is Stripe in New Zealand.

rules.low: Domestic card 2.65% + NZ$0.30 (standard pricing page); Stripe handles Connect pricing, so no payout fees
rules.mid: Domestic card 2.7% + NZ$0.30 (Connect pricing page, marketplaces where Stripe handles pricing)
rules.high: International card 3.7% + NZ$0.30 (Connect page), plus 2% currency conversion where the guest pays in another currency (Stay), plus platform-priced Connect fees: 0.25% + NZ$0.25 per payout and NZ$2 per active payee a month

payment.rent: Rent can go by bank direct debit instead: NZ BECS through Stripe, 1% + NZ$0.40 capped at NZ$4.00 a debit; or by plain bank transfer that the app only records.
unverified: Which card rate a Connect marketplace pays: the standard page shows 2.65% + NZ$0.30 and the Connect page 2.7% + NZ$0.30 (both open on 2026-10-18). Ask Stripe.
Whether Stripe's 0.25% funds-routing fee stacks with the per-payout fee when the platform handles pricing; not included
Whether GST or VAT is charged on Stripe's fees (moot here, since all figures exclude tax)

unverified: Which Stripe card rate a Connect marketplace pays (2.65% or 2.7% domestic) and whether the 0.25% funds-routing fee stacks.
Hetzner showed 'This product is currently unavailable' on every cloud plan on 18 Oct 2026, so the Hetzner setups (Office low, Construct and Studio low) may not be orderable today.

OVHcloud: which OVH company bills a buyer outside Australia (its other catalogues list the same VPS at US$10 a month), and the price of the IPv4 address that Auckland Local Zone servers must pay for (shown only in the control panel).
Server capacity per user (marketplace servers, Social app servers, Office co-editing, mail and video, the design tools' sync servers) is not load tested.
Spare Social low case: serving video from Cloudflare R2 under Cloudflare's CDN terms, and free PhotoDNA scanning (needs an application).
Self-hosted video transcoding speed on the Hetzner AX42 needs a test encode.
Didit ID checks: the 500 free checks a month end on 1 Nov 2026 (US$10 of credit a month after that); the US$0.33 per check used here stays.
Many price pages show '$' without naming the currency (Cloudflare, Twilio, Postmark, Mapbox, Algolia, Sentry and others); USD is assumed.
Apple Developer fee waiver for non-profits, and whether native iPhone apps ship at all (piece K04).
ACC work levy and Working Safer levy rates in the people on-costs.
Spare OS: monthly update size is measured on one example image (Aurora, 15 Sep to 13 Oct 2026); downloads per install and machine life are assumptions.
Incumbent figures: Uber's 28% is an illustration in its driver guide; agents' 3 to 4% comes from calculator sites; Fiverr's 20% from secondary sources.
Our own assumptions, not research: the example amounts, 10 active users per list-app transaction, a 12-month tenancy, and the pilot team size.
checker_corrections_applied: Stripe Connect page rates (2.7% domestic, 3.7% international) used for the middle and high cases; 2.65% only for the low case.
ClickSend low SMS rate NZ$0.1227 (NZ$20 top-up tier) instead of NZ$0.1014, which needs a NZ$13,000 top-up.
OVHcloud VPS-2 2027 at A$14.00 with no commitment plus the mandatory A$0.90 backup, instead of A$11.90 (12 months upfront) and A$1.00.
Hetzner prices with the EUR 0.50 primary IPv4 included where the page includes it.
Postmark: per-email overage plus the US$15 plan in the high case, with no second per-email charge inside the plan in the move family.

Stream Chat priced as its flat US$499 a month (1,001 to 10,000 monthly users), not US$0.09 per user; Meilisearch Cloud dropped from the list high baseline; Sumsub's US$149 minimum used instead of Veriff's.
Azure egress at the default routing rate US$0.12 per GB.
Clerk's US$0.02 per user dropped from the kit per-member high case.
Azure Postgres backup storage is free up to the provisioned size (kit high baseline).
Mapbox geocoding instead of Google in the list high case.
Spare Social high case servers on AWS (2 x m7g.xlarge), not OVH; transcoding box treated as a fixed cost, not a per-minute cost.
OVH object storage priced per GiB, not per GB.
Spare OS high download 7.2 GB a month (a 30.44-day month, not 28 days); Sentry usage inside the 50,000 included errors costs nothing; the OVH mirror is not counted twice.
People on-costs compound on holiday pay (1.1261, not 1.1219).
Didit free tier ends 1 Nov 2026, so the low ID check is US$0.33, not US$0.
